CHAPTER: R.S.C., 1985, c. E-2
TITLE: Canada Elections Act

PART I
DEFINITIONS
Marginal note: Definitions
2 In this Act,
(a) elector means a person who
(i) is a Canadian citizen, and
(ii) is eighteen years of age or older on polling day;
(b) returning officer means the officer appointed under section 24 to conduct an election in an electoral district.

PART II
ELECTION OFFICERS
Marginal note: Appointment
3 (1) The Chief Electoral Officer shall appoint a returning officer for each electoral district.
Marginal note: Vacancy
(2) Where a vacancy occurs in the office of returning officer, the Chief Electoral Officer shall
(a) appoint a replacement without delay; and
(b) notify the Speaker of the House of Commons of the vacancy and the appointment.

DELEGATION OF DUTIES
3.1 A returning officer may authorize an assistant returning officer to exercise any of the powers or perform any of the duties conferred on the returning officer under this Act.

4 An elector who is unable to attend at a polling station on polling day because of illness may apply for a special ballot, and the application shall include
(a) the elector's full name and address;
(b) the elector's date of birth; and
(c) the elector's signature.

COMING INTO FORCE
Marginal note: Coming into force
5 This Act comes into force on a day to be fixed by order of the Governor in Council.
